title: SynkLoader Malware Spreads Through Microsoft Teams Phishing and Steals Windows Passwords
content_md: A previously undocumented malware loader, dubbed SynkLoader, that combines Python, C#, and native C++ components to evade detection, steal Windows credentials, and enable deep network access. First spotted on August 18, 2026, during an EDR alert triggered by a suspicious scheduled task, the malware appears to have been compiled around July 28, 2026, and shows hallmarks of ransomware or initial-access-broker tooling. The infection began with a Microsoft Teams message from an attacker posing as “IT Service Desk ,” using a spoofed @company.onmicrosoft.com address to appear legitimate. SynkLoader Malware Spreads Through Microsoft Teams The impersonator convinced the target to download an MSI installer, disguised as a “PowerShell Cleaner,” from an Azure Blob Storage URL, lending the payload false credibility by leveraging Microsoft’s own infrastructure. Once executed, the MSI drops a PowerShell script that runs entirely in memory using nested Invoke-Expression and ScriptBlock::Create calls, decrypting an AES-CBC payload before deploying a full embedded Python environment to %AppData% . The content of the fl\ang subdirectory (Source: expel) The core loader script, ss.py , beacons to one of several C2 domains including neversoftmain[.]net and rootfarmapp[.]net using a modified ChaCha20 cipher with altered “Sigma” constants, encrypting traffic with a randomly generated victim ID as the key.
